sentences.text:
2 The petitioners - accused Nos.2 to 8 along with accused No.1 have been charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of D P Act.
2.

The summary of the charge sheet is that, the marriage of the defacto complainant was solemnized with the accused No.1 on 6.5.2018, and thereafter, the accused subjected her to cruelty both physically and mentally, and also demanded to bring money from the parental home.

On 18.6.2019,
the accused herein forced the defacto complainant to leave the matrimonial home.
On 16.1.2021, the accused No.1 came to the parental home, picked up a quarrel, abused her in filthy language and also assaulted her.
The learned Magistrate, after accepting the charge sheet, took the cognizance of the aforesaid offences and issued summons.
Taking exception of the same, the accused Nos.2 to 8 are before this Court.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners - accused Nos.2 to 8 and the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent - State.
4.

Perusal of the charge sheet material indicates that, the accused have forced the defacto complainant to leave the matrimonial home on 18.6.2019, and thereafter the defacto complainant was residing at parental home, and on 16.1.2021 , the accused No.1 came to the parental home,
abused her in filthy language and assaulted her.

5. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar, (2022) 6 SCC 599 has held that the relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar, (2022) 6 SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, there is no specific allegation against accused Nos.2 to 8 except general and omnibus allegations to constitute the above offences.

6. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of A.P. v. M. Madhusudhan Rao [(2008) 15 SCC 582] has held as follows:
"30.

entities.text: State of A.P. v. M. Madhusudhan Rao [(2008) 15 SCC 582]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Time and again, the object and importance of prompt lodging of the first information report has been highlighted.
Delay in lodging the first information report, more often than not, results in embellishment and exaggeration, which is a creature of an afterthought.

A delayed report not only gets bereft of the advantage of spontaneity, the danger of the introduction of a coloured version, an exaggerated account of the incident or a concocted story as a result of deliberations and consultations, also creeps in, casting a serious doubt on its veracity.

Therefore, it is essential that the delay in lodging the report should be satisfactorily explained."
7.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that, the delay in filing the FIR should be explained, and in the absence of such explanation, the FIR lodged becomes an afterthought.

No explanation is offered by the defacto complainant for the delay in lodging the FIR insofar as it relates to accused herein against whom, it is alleged that they along with accused No.1 have thrown out the defacto complainant from the matrimonial home on 6.5.2018.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
